content.text: Would it be better to just ignore "lastModified" for the purpose of mutating requests?
I don't understand this ticket. Is it JUST the lastModified field that causes this or the GET-PUT-PUT? If its the GET-PUT-PUT operations, shouldn't the error message be more generalized?

Fedora doesn't track the order of HTTP request methods as they come in, it only cares about preventing conflicts. It uses the lastModified triple to determine whether the RDF in a PUT request is based on the latest version in the repository. Otherwise, there could be a situation like this:
T+00:00:00 client1 GET /foo (lastModified T-08:30:50)
T+00:00:01 client2 GET /foo (lastModified T-08:30:50)
T+00:00:05 client1 PUT /foo (lastModified T-08:30:50) success, lastModified updated to T+00:00:05
T+00:00:06 client2 PUT /foo (lastModified T-08:30:50) client2 wipes out client1's changes
This ticket concerns the clarity of the error message and the suitability of the HTTP status code that result when an attempt is made to do this.
To be clear, given the vagaries of network transit and ntp, Fedora
can't
order requests.
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/pull/810
See code review comments.
Give this a shot,
https://github.com/robyj/fcrepo4/pull/1
I talked to
and he is going to merge your pull request
. Hopefully that will finish this off.
If not let me know what is needed. cheers.
Now that we support -Dfcrepo.properties.management="relaxed" for overriding server managed triples, this one should be resolved.
I'm closing it.

When updating a container via HTTP PUT, the value of the `fedora:lastModified` triple must match its current counterpart in the repository, otherwise an HTTP 400 error is returned with the following message:
Could not remove triple containing predicate
http://fedora.info/definitions/v4/repository#lastModified
to node /book

This should really be a 409 (Conflict) error with an improved message. I would propose something like: "Cannot update the container as the supplied RDF is out-of-date based on the value of its fedora:lastModified triple."
Background:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/issues/800#issuecomment-104694026
